message.content:
I'm ending my turn without building. Putting hotels on St. Charles Place and States Avenue would cost $100 each and raise their rent from $625 to $750. But each hotel sends 4 houses back to the bank, and the bank only has 2 left. Those freed houses would let gpt-6.1-sol build up the green set and Park Place/Boardwalk, so it's better to keep them tied up.

I'm also keeping my $140 as a buffer after paying $390 rent on North Carolina Avenue.
message.reasoning:
With $140 left after rent, I'm weighing whether to build hotels on St Charles or States—each costs $100 and converts 4 houses into a hotel worth $750 rent. But doing so returns those houses to the bank, potentially letting an opponent use them to upgrade Pacific/NC/Penn or Park Place/Boardwalk, so holding onto the houses as a shortage strategy might be smarter.

Since the bank only has 2 houses and an opponent has $545 to buy them, releasing more houses by hoteling would help them too much. I should keep my cash thin and just end the turn, since I can't cover their hotel-level rents anyway.
